source.publication_title: Rhode Island wildlife camera trap survey 2018 to 2023

public_methods.geographic_scope: Rhode Island, USA, statewide design divided into western and eastern sections
public_methods.survey_seasons: six winter, five summer and one spring
public_methods.paired_camera_spacing_m: approximately 20-130 m across associated studies, typically 50-100 m
public_methods.deployment_fields_described: start/end operation dates, camera location, coordinates, Site and camera IDs
public_methods.detection_fields_described: Site, camera identifier, timestamp and species identity
public_methods.package_version_note: v3 reports one row per image, not a predeclared independent detection event; image bursts must not be treated as independent observations

gates.reason: Rhode Island independent long-term camera dataset not used in E2-E4, Snapshot Japan or the wild-pig alternative route
Zenodo v3 describes separate deployment/observation CSVs with stable Site+Camera identifiers and date/time; compressed member names and exact fields unverified
two cameras per site in later survey seasons may create paired within-context contrasts; must show physically distinct west/east regimes and paired camera/protocol overlap without confounding

individual camera identity is described as retained, unlike earlier paired datasets. Cameras 50-100m apart do not observe the same animal passage automatically: detection identifiability must be proven for matched site/occasion repeats without conflating placement/activity
249 total survey sites, but split-specific unique physical counts and repeat nesting are unverified
12 seasonal survey periods span 2018-2023; >=6 distinct months and matched seasonal exposure in each west/east split have not been measured
candidate remains unqualified, no response opening or model fitting

decision.next_step: response-blind ZIP member names and CSV header-only precheck, then independently adjudicate Site/Camera/year-season/start/end/time fields before any biological values
decision.stop_rule: if paired camera identity, deployment linkage, geographic regimes, or feasible detection-identification design is absent, stop before opening focal rows

interpretation.supported: first newly surfaced E5 candidate with multi-year exposure and explicit camera-member identifiers in both deployment and detection descriptions; plausible paired-camera calibration route
not_supported: claim that two cameras 50-100 m apart share animal passages
claim that G3 or G4 has passed
claim of >=6 months in each geographically heldout split

identifiability_obligation.obligation: two uncalibrated time-varying camera processes possess a common multiplicative gauge with latent activity; member identities/headers alone cannot pass original G4
identifiability_obligation.possible_escape_requires: independently calibrated detection, actual common-passage co-detection histories or a separately demonstrated repeated-occasion detection identification path
